newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Salomon rates China Eastern as Buy.
newsitem.headline: Salomon rates China Eastern as Buy.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said it rated China Eastern Airlines Corp Ltd as a buy in its latest Asia-Pacific Airline Industry Review.

The review said Shanghai-based China Eastern, one of China's three largest airlines and the first Chinese carrier to be listed in Hong Kong, has long term, high growth potential and cheap relative valuations.

"Robust" traffic growth projections and a favourable, though regulated, domestic and international market, should allow it to produce earnings growth close to 20 per cent in fiscal year 1998, the review said.

Further cause for optimism was the expectation of China Eastern being given approval to renew or make further additions to capacity, although scope remains for domestic competition which may lead to yield pressure, it added.

China Eastern's fleet also has "enormous long term utilisation potential" because current aircraft utilisation is 5.6 hours per day, half that of regional competitors such as Cathay Pacific Ltd, the review said.

The carrier's business strategy was also highlighted which includes utilising more modern and fuel efficient aircraft, raising service standards, optimising flight operations, enhancing maintenance capability and expanding the international and domestic sales network.
The only other airline to also win a Buy rating is Air New Zealand which will be able to grow earnings without necessarily increasing revenue, the report said.

The other listed airlines in the review, Cathay Pacific Airways, Singapore Airlines, Qantas Airways Ltd, Malaysia Airline System Bhd and Thai Airways International, all receive Hold ratings. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax 5017
